entries.proposition: Registration: PROSPERO protocol registered 1 October 2024; search run 1 October 2024 and updated 9 April 2025.
entries.snippet: The systematic review protocol was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) on October 1, 2024 (CRD42024569173).

experimental_context.system: meta-analysis of seven studies of NIRS cerebral saturation around red-cell transfusion in preterm infants, liberal versus restrictive haemoglobin thresholds
experimental_context.comparator: pre versus post transfusion within study arms; subgroup contrast between threshold groups across studies

entries.proposition: Classification rule: studies were assigned to liberal or restrictive by their stated threshold, approximately 10-13 g/dL versus 7-11 g/dL, with overlap between the two ranges.
entries.snippet: Definitions of “liberal” and “restrictive” were consistent with the high or low haemoglobin threshold (approximately 10–13 g/dL vs. 7–11 g/dL), used in established trials [4–7].

entries.proposition: Attrition of eligibility: of 24 studies with before-and-after crSO2, 4 had no formal protocol and 13 gave insufficient detail, leaving 7.
entries.snippet: Twenty-four studies reported before and after changes in crSO2, however, four of these studies used no formal transfusion protocol, and thirteen did not report sufficient information to classify as either “liberal” or “restrictive.”

entries.proposition: Primary result: crSO2 rose 6.40 points under restrictive thresholds (n = 357 events) and 2.75 under liberal (n = 220); the subgroup difference has Q = 4.19, p = 0.04.
entries.snippet: Subgroup analysis indicated statistically significant differences between liberal (n = 220) and restrictive (n = 357) groups (Q = 4.19, df = 1, p = 0.04) with a greater magnitude of change under a restrictive threshold (shown in Fig. 2).

entries.proposition: The conclusion reads the larger restrictive-group increase as enhanced physiological benefit, in the Discussion; in the same Clinical Implications the authors say the clinical meaning of a crSO2 change is undefined.
entries.snippet: Firstly, a clinically relevant change in crSO2 remains undefined and the effect of a relative increase in crSO2 by 2.75% (liberal threshold) compared to 6.4% (restrictive threshold) is unknown.

entries.proposition: NIRS-guided treatment in a cited trial reduced cerebral hypoxia by 58 percent without improving death or brain injury; the authors say increases in cerebral oxygenation may not predict improved outcomes.
entries.snippet: This suggests, as with the transfusion setting, NIRS-detected increases in cerebral oxygenation may not predict improved clinical outcomes.
